{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[ja:正五位]]

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.

This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.
== External Links == * [https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/document?lawid=215IO0000000325] - {{ill|e-Gov|ja|e-Gov法令検索}} * [{{NDLDC|787949/168}} {{ill|Official Rank Table|ja|官位相当表}}] - National Diet Library Digital Collections

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...
== See Also == * {{ill|Daiō|ja|大夫}} * {{ill|Uji rank system|ja|氏爵}} * {{ill|Annual rank system|ja|年爵}} * {{ill|Honorary ranks|ja|栄爵}} * {{ill|巡爵|ja|巡爵}} * {{ill|Black-crowned night heron|ja|ゴイサギ}} – A {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}} anecdote where a {{ill|Daigo Tennō|ja|醍醐天皇}}’s decree elevated a captured bird to Shōgoi.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

{{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''正五位'''（しょうごい）とは、[[日本]]の[[位階]]及び[[神階]]における位のひとつ。[[従四位]]の下、[[従五位]]の上に位する。[[贈位]]の場合、贈正五位という。
== 概要 == 正五位は、[[律令制]]下において上下にわけられ、[[官位]]相当では主に[[京官]]、特に[[次官]]ないし[[判官]]相当の[[位階]]として充てられた。例えば[[太政官]]の[[弁官|左右中弁や小弁]]、[[八省]]の[[大輔]]、[[大判事]]、[[職]]の[[大膳職|大膳大夫]]、[[近衛府]]の少将、[[衛門府]]、[[兵衛府]]の[[督]]などが挙げられる。
[[武家]]においては、[[鎌倉時代]]に[[北条氏]]の一門が叙せられたほか、[[豊臣氏]]の政権下における[[大名]]の位階としても叙位がなされたが、[[江戸時代]]には[[従四位|従四位下]]や[[従五位|従五位下]]の叙位が集中したため、幕藩体制の中の[[武家]]で正五位に叙せられた者は少ない。[[江戸時代]]の主な叙任者は[[宮廷]]の[[地下官人]]や[[親王家]]・[[摂家|五摂家]]・[[清華家]]などに仕えた[[諸大夫]]であり、[[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]関係者の専用の位階ということができる。
[[明治|明治時代]]以降には、[[叙位条例]]が制定されたことに伴い、従四位以上は[[勅授]]、正五位以下は、[[奏授]]により位階を授けられることとなった<ref group="注釈">叙位条例第3条にて「凡ソ位ハ従四位以上ハ勅授トシ宮内大臣之ヲ奉ス正五位以下ハ奏授トシ宮内大臣之ヲ宣ス」と規定された。</ref>。特に、明治以降は[[明治維新|維新]]に功労のあった[[志士]]について、主に[[家老]]職にない中堅・下級武士の者が多く追贈され、歴史上の人物としては、[[間宮林蔵]]（[[1904年]]（[[明治]]37年）[[4月22日]]）贈位された他、[[鎌倉時代]]、[[金沢文庫]]の創設など文化的な功績を残した[[北条実時]]（[[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）[[11月10日]]）が追贈の対象とされた。なお、政府の[[官吏]]に対する位階としては[[内閣法制局長官]]や[[政務次官]]、[[軍人]]については[[少将]]が正五位に叙されるなど、中堅[[官僚]]・[[軍人]]の位階として位置づけられた。 現行制度では、[[位階]]は死没者に対する[[栄典]]として与えられることとなっており、[[大学]]・[[短期大学]]・[[高等専門学校]]において[[名誉教授]]の[[称号]]を受けた者、民間企業の[[経営者]]のうち秀逸な業績のある者、あるいは、公務員として功績のある者や、[[旭日中綬章]]など（旧勲三等）を受けた芸術家、学術研究に功績のある[[学者]]、[[芸能]]・文化活動に功績のある[[芸能人]]などが叙せられている。

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
== Recipients of Posthumous Shōgoi (Zōshōgoi) After the Meiji Restoration == * {{ill|1882|ja|1882年}} (Meiji 15), June 3<ref>『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.2</ref> ''' {{ill|Hayashi Shihei|ja|林子平}}, {{ill|Satō Nobuhiro|ja|佐藤信淵}} * {{ill|1883|ja|1883年}} (Meiji 16), August 6<ref name="zoui3">『贈位諸賢伝 増補版 上』特旨贈位年表 p.3</ref> - {{ill|Sakurayama Chikatoshi|ja|桜山茲俊}} * ...

[[Category:new pages]] {{出典の明記|date=2015年8月}} '''Shōgoi''' (正五位) is one of the ranks in the {{ill|Japanese|ja|日本}} {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}} and [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai (divine ranks)]]. It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. Posthumous ranks for this level are referred to as ''Zōshōgoi''.
== Overview ==
Shōgoi, under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}, was divided into upper and lower grades. In terms of {{ill|official ranks|ja|官位|1=Kan'i system}}, it corresponded primarily to {{ill|Kyōkan|ja|京官}} (capitals officers), especially positions such as {{ill|Benkan|ja|弁官}} ({{ill|Chūben|ja|左右中弁}} or {{ill|Shōben|ja|少弁}}) of the {{ill|Daijō-kan|ja|太政官}}, {{ill|Daibu|ja|大輔}} of the {{ill|Eight Ministries|ja|八省}}, {{ill|Ōbanshi|ja|大判事}}, {{ill|Ōzen-shoku|ja|大膳職}} (Ōzen-daibu), {{ill|Shōshō|ja|少将}} of the {{ill|Konoe Guards|ja|近衛府}}, and {{ill|Ōkan|ja|衛門府}}. These positions marked the middle-tier bureaucratic status.
In the {{ill|samurai|ja|武家}} class, the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ja|北条氏}} received this rank during the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, while it was granted to {{ill|daimyō|ja|大名}} during the {{ill|Toyotomi regime|ja|豊臣氏}}. However, during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, appointments to Shōgoi decreased as focus shifted to {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Jūgoi|ja|従五位|1=Junior Fifth Rank}}. In this era, the rank was mainly awarded to {{ill|court officials|ja|宮廷}} like {{ill|Chikashōnin|ja|地下官人}} serving the {{ill|Imperial court|ja|朝廷}}, {{ill|Shinnōke|ja|親王家}}, {{ill|Gosekke|ja|五摂家}}, and {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}.
From the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治}}, with the enactment of the {{ill|Rank Grant Ordinance|ja|叙位条例}}, ranks above {{ill|Jūshi'i|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}} were granted by imperial decree, while Shōgoi and below were conferred by submission (奏授). This rank often recognized mid-level samurai, {{ill|military officers|ja|軍人}}, and {{ill|bureaucrats|ja|官僚}}, especially those with notable contributions during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}. Historical figures awarded the posthumous Shōgoi include {{ill|Mamiya Rinzō|ja|間宮林蔵}} (granted in {{ill|1904|ja|1904年}}) and {{ill|Hōjō Sanetoki|ja|北条実時}} (granted in {{ill|1915|ja|1915年}}) for cultural accomplishments like founding the {{ill|Kanazawa Library|ja|金沢文庫}}.
Under the current system, ranks are conferred posthumously as honors. Recipients often include distinguished {{ill|university|ja|大学}} and {{ill|college|ja|短期大学}} professors, {{ill|business leaders|ja|経営者}}, {{ill|civil servants|ja|公務員}}, and notable {{ill|scholars|ja|学者}}, {{ill|artists|ja|芸術家}}, and {{ill|performers|ja|芸能人}} who received awards like the {{ill|Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon|ja|旭日中綬章}}.
